newsitem.title: TAIWAN: Taiwan sets up Hong Kong affairs bureau.
newsitem.headline: Taiwan sets up Hong Kong affairs bureau.

text.p: Taipei on Thursday approved setting up a bureau to supervise Taiwan government-related organisations in Hong Kong ahead of the handover of the British colony to China.

"The cabinet has approved the regulations governing the establishment of the Hong Kong Affairs Bureau, which would become effective immediately," Chang Shu-ting, a liaison chief of the Mainland Affairs Council, told Reuters.
The bureau would run government-related organisations in Hong Kong. These institutions would continue operations in Hong Kong using their existing titles to avoid political sensitivities, he said.
Hong Kong returns to Chinese rule at midnight on June 30.
Communist China, which views Nationalist-ruled Taiwan as a rebel-held province since a civil war split them in 1949, has said it will allow Taiwan's offices in Hong Kong to continue operating.
But the organisations are forbidden to use titles which would give the impression of another China or an independent Taiwan.
China has warned against full independence of Taiwan.

Currently, the foreign ministry's visa office in Hong Kong uses the title Chung Hwa Travel Service and the Government Information Office's Hong Kong unit is known as Kwang Hwa Information and Culture Centre.
The economics ministry's office uses the name Far Eastern Trade Service.
Council officials said the titles used by these organisations were not politically sensitive and should be allowed to continue their operations after Hong Kong was handed back to China.
